name: BEST OF THREE.
idea: WORLD: angoothi dhoondhna after the pheras, broadcast live like a world final. A polished brass paraat about 45 cm across, milky water, a few blush and ivory petals, an oxblood shamiana with warm fairy lights (plum for the one rhodium chain). Only hands and forearms: hers with fresh mehendi and a red kalava thread, his with an ivory sherwani cuff and a kalava; never chooda, bangles or other rings. Only waterproof-tagged pieces go into the milk, so every plate proves waterproof without a claims panel. TEN BROADCAST MOMENTS, never the same splash twice: Match (cards 1-5) the burst, the wire cam, the photo finish, the decision (a victory fist), the trophy lift under a petal shower; Rematch (cards 6-10) the replay, day five's search, the sore loser's time-out ('best of four?'), the fix (he lets her win), the prize-giving (she runs the house). Cameras and light change with the moment: flash freeze, top-down daylight, a single lamp, low backlit hero, flash with falling petals, plum macro, a milk-line horizon, low diya-side light, raking tungsten, amber rim. WORDS: each Velista headline is the commentator's call, and every call is literally true of the piece: TOO CLOSE TO CALL (the ring's two ends), NOTHING TO LOSE (no stones), BEST OF THREE (three clear pears, then mint), DAY FIVE (a Test match's last day and the wedding's), BEST OF FOUR? (BUY4), MATCH FIXED (a thrown game and a settled rishta). The score lives in Jost because Velista has no digits. GRAPHIC SYSTEM: a hand-made match-day kit (live dot and score strip with chalk tallies, the call, one proof device born from the plate, the F2 card on cocoa), never a real channel's graphics. BUILD: the hands, milk, splash and the piece are one generated plate; a plate whose piece drifts is regenerated, never composited, retouched or moved (hard rule), so construction never changes. MOTION: cards 1, 3, 5, 6 and 10 animate in Kling 3.0 (the burst, the reach, the petal shower, the falling drop, the still milk round the raised arm), image-to-video from the approved still only; the piece never moves or changes; type moves in HTML.
insight: Every season our buyer stands at the edge of the same paraat: the one wedding ritual whose whole climax is finding a piece of jewellery (angoothi dhoondhna; eki beki in Gujarati homes). Two hands, a paraat of milk, one ring, the family screaming, and a rule everyone already knows: best of three, and whoever wins runs the house. The rule is our offer (BUY3), the milk is our proof (waterproof shown, not claimed), and India already watches this game the way it watches cricket, with a commentator in every family. The game is about finding a small thing nobody could see, which is exactly what these slow-stock pieces need: to be found, this wedding season, before the next function.
textualGraphic: THE MATCH-DAY KIT, hand-made, never a real channel's, league's or app's graphics; at most four text elements per card, set with the restraint of the live lotus Story (tracked Jost labels, Cormorant italic asides, one huge Velista call). (1) SCORE STRIP, top-left x 72, y 84 (Story y 270): a 10 px terracotta #B5502F live dot (pulsing at 1 Hz in HTML), then Jost 500 caps 26 px, tracking .16em, bone #F4F0E8 on dark plates, ink #1A1614 on milk, at most 40 characters, e.g. 'ROUND 1 · HER 1 · HIM 0'. Her tallies are SVG chalk strokes, 2 px x 34 px, 9 px apart, saffron #E8A33A, edges roughened with feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap; HIM's slot is an empty 18 px hairline ring. The strip advances card by card, so the carousel reads as one match and a rematch while each card still reads alone, and the gags live inside it (WIRE CAM, UNDER REVIEW, DECISION, STONES LOST 0, DAY 5, TIME-OUT, HIM 1 struck out to 0, HOUSE: HERS). (2) THE CALL: Velista caps 100-120 px Feed, 116-136 px Story, line-height .98, tracking .02em, ligatures off, the winning words in saffron on dark or coral-deep #C8664A on milk; never digits, ₹, middle dots or dashes; a Cormorant Garamond italic 500 second beat at 44-48 px in gold-light #E4C889 or coral-deep, deadpan and lower-case. (3) ONE PROOF DEVICE born from the plate, different on every card and always carrying a listing fact in mm or a tag-backed claim: SIZE GUN (1: a speed-gun arc of five segments, US 5 to US 9, all lit, 'READS: ALL FIVE'), RIPPLE TEXT (2: SVG circles traced on the plate's own ripples, Jost on textPath), PHOTO FINISH (3: one 1 px saffron finish line through the gap between two fingertips, plus a bracket over the ring's two ends), TWO-ROW SCALE BAR (4: the COW FOR SCALE graft, 'PARAAT · ABOUT 45 CM' over 450 px and the band over a 6 px stub at the same 1 px per mm), ROUNDS TO PRIZE (5: leaders from three clear pears to ROUND 1-3 and from the mint pear to the offer), TWO DROPS (6: a replay freeze frame, milk falls off, cubic zirconia stays), SEARCH RETICLE (7: crosshair and range rings, a 10 mm target in one paraat), SLO-MO CAM (8: the O of FOUR is a same-picture loupe on the pair; no prices, totals or sums), TOI ET MOI TAGS (9: his end, her end), HOUSE RULES (10: the offer as a numbered list with one rule for him). Leaders are 2 px and end in a 10 px open circle on metal, never on a stone. (4) THE F2 CARD on a cocoa #3B2620 scrim: logo_white 56 px, name Jost 500 26 px .2em, price Cormorant 56 px, one line Jost 26 px, offer box Jost 500 26 px .14em in a 2 px hairline with gold-light diamond separators; Feed y 880-1200, Story y 1000-1250; no CTA button in the image. A trust line sits under the offer box, right-aligned, Jost 500 caps 20 px .14em bone at 80%, ON on every card: 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY' (owner ruling, 20 Nov 2026); never a delivery time. The offer box carries the BASKET METER: three 14 px saffron chalk circles, the first filled, before 'THIS + ANY TWO · BUY3 · 20% OFF' (card 8: four circles before 'THIS + ANY THREE · BUY4 · 30% OFF'). Type is drawn on the dark half of the frame; the splash, the milk crown and the piece are never lettered over.
brandFeatures: The F2 card is the anchor on every card: Naira wordmark (logo_white, with its tulip I) on cocoa, name, price, one listing line, offer box 'THIS + ANY TWO · BUY3 · 20% OFF' after the basket meter (card 8: 'THIS + ANY THREE · BUY4 · 30% OFF'; on card 10 the house rules replace the box and rule 2 carries the meter), with 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY' under it. Type is locked to Velista, Cormorant Garamond and Jost. The camp is a running joke on 'Petite': the whole game is finding something small in something big (a 10 mm charm in a 45 cm paraat), and the devices say so in millimetres. Hands carry mehendi and a red kalava, never another piece, so the Naira piece is the only jewellery in every frame. Sign-off on every ad, as the Meta description line and the carousel's last words: 'Naira Petite. Whoever finds it, keeps it.'
palette: Plate: milk white, polished brass, blush and ivory petals (never on card 9), mehendi reddish-brown, red kalava. Grounds: oxblood #6E1F23 shamiana for the gold-tone and green pieces (cards 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10), plum #4A2540 for the rhodium Serpentine (card 6), milk white for the wire cam (card 2). Type: bone #F4F0E8 on dark, ink #1A1614 on milk; saffron #E8A33A for HER's tallies, the finish line and winning words on dark, coral-deep #C8664A on milk; terracotta #B5502F only for the live dot; gold-light #E4C889 for beats, hairline boxes and offer separators; cocoa #3B2620 under every card. The piece is always the most saturated or brightest thing in its frame: green on oxblood, clear on plum, gold on white, satin in lamplight.
sellLever: BEST OF THREE is BUY3: the ritual's own rule is the offer, so cards 5 and 10 close on it and every primary text carries 'any three, 20% off with BUY3' before character 125. The ladder runs through the match: BUY3 on the trophy (5), BUY4 on 'best of four?' (8), where the call 'BEST OF FOUR?' and the offer box 'THIS + ANY THREE · BUY4 · 30% OFF' carry the step from three to four; no basket, total, saving or sum is ever printed (hard rule); all three tiers as HOUSE RULES (10). Reason to buy now: this is the wedding week the pieces are shown surviving (haldi, sangeet, milk, day five), not a fake countdown. Funnel: PAIN 4, 7 · OUTCOME 2, 3, 9 · OBJECTION 1, 6 · OFFER 5, 8, 10; layers EDUCATION 2, 3 · TRUST 1, 4, 6, 7 · SELL 5, 8, 9, 10; cards 8 and 9 also run to men 18-24 as the gift. Stock logic: the anchors are the deepest slow stock (Woven 88, Verdant 58, Brushed 58, Triple Coil gold 20), while the thin pieces (Baroque Bloom 10, Tubogas gold 8, Droplet silver 11) sit on cards where one sale matters and nothing promises a count.
carouselText: Rematch: best of three again, and whoever wins runs the house. Any three, 20% off with BUY3; any four, 30% off with BUY4. Five waterproof pieces, every one in stock. Free insured shipping, cash on delivery. Naira Petite. Whoever finds it, keeps it.
changes: Pushed the words from results to commentary: every Velista headline is now the broadcast's call and literally true of the piece. Card 2 'ROUND TWO: HERS AGAIN.' (samey with card 1) became 'VISIBLE FROM THE CHHAT.', the wire cam's boast and the outcome she wants. Card 3 'ALMOST TOUCHING.' collided with k10's card 10 and became 'TOO CLOSE TO CALL.', with a PHOTO FINISH device (a 1 px saffron finish line through the gap between the fingertips); the unlisted 'under 1 mm' gap is gone from the type, which now says 'almost touching' (the listing's words) and the listed 6.6 mm teardrop. Card 4 'NO STONES TO LOSE.' became 'NOTHING TO LOSE.' (the fearless team's phrase and the ring's bill of materials), with a sharper pain (a stone lost mid-sangeet, the baraat spent searching). Card 7 'FOUND: ONE SMALL CHARM.' became 'DAY FIVE. STILL BRIGHT.' with the beat 'by day five, most jewellery looks like day five.', and the macro now turns the paraat into a white sea with the fingertip as a lighthouse. Card 8 'EK AUR ROUND?' became 'BEST OF FOUR?' (the sore loser changing the rules is BUY4), the bill gains a '+ ₹189' margin note and the beat says a fourth piece adds about ₹190; its light moved from on-camera flash (k06's signature) to a low diya-side glow that suits brushed satin, and the prompt now puts the palm left so the bill has room. Card 9 'LET HER WIN.' became 'MATCH FIXED.' (a thrown game and a settled rishta); the tags now say 'clear cubic zirconia' so no 'emerald' word reaches the type. Card 1 keeps its call and gains the SIZE GUN, a speed-gun arc that reads US 5 to US 9 and lights all five in motion; its beat stays clear of k04's 'NOBODY KNOWS HER RING SIZE.'. Card 5 gains a petal shower (phoolon ki baarish) for the trophy lift. Card 6 is now animated: the milk bead swells, falls and plinks while the stone stays, the proof playing out in real time. Card 10's prompt now leaves the right third calm for the rules. Every score strip gained a live dot and was cut to 40 characters so it fits the 936 px measure; '(he found it first)' moved to a second line. Kept as they were: 'ROUND ONE: HERS.', 'BEST OF THREE.', 'ONE DROP IS MILK.', 'HOUSE RULES.' and the ten pictures' construction locks. FLAG FOR THE OWNER: concept-50 RULINGS §6 says every ad carries 'FREE INSURED SHIPPING · CASH ON DELIVERY', but this step's hard rule 5 says never free shipping, and on 20 Nov the store still charged ₹150 below ₹3,000 (a BUY3 basket is about ₹2,400). The F2 card has the delivery line slot built in, switched off, to turn on once the checkout matches and the rule is settled. Build: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll/81f6e48f-a340-5398-99b2-f7e22fb69d37/scratchpad/k03/k03_v2.json, generated by build_v2.py in the same folder with copy checks. truth: card 1 prompt, the ring (about 20 mm outside) is a little wider than the fingertip pad that grips it, not narrower, so it is not drawn undersized. truth: card 2 prompt, a 25 mm hoop is about one and a half times the width of the finger it rests on; 'two fingers side by side' (about 32 mm) would draw it about 1.3x. truth: card 3 prompt, 'composed like the reaching hands of a Renaissance ceiling fresco' became 'two bare reaching hands whose index fingers almost touch': the fresco cue invites painted figures and faces; the near-touch idea is unchanged. truth: card 5 prompt, the 18 mm earring is about two thirds of the thumb's top joint (about 28 mm, the house referent), not 'a little shorter', which drew it about 1.4x. truth: card 7 primary text, 'still bright after haldi' implied turmeric-stain resistance, which no tag backs; now 'still bright after sangeet and milk' (waterproof and tarnish free are tagged). truth: card 8 prompt, the card's lock is pasted whole again ('1 pair of chunky huggie hoops'; the word stays out of all copy), and each 14 mm earring is about a sixth of a man's palm width, not a quarter (about 1.5x). truth: checked and kept: every piece in the milk is waterproof-tagged; variants shown are in stock (Droplet ring silver 11, Tubogas gold US 6-8, Triple Coil gold 20); live prices; BUY2/BUY3/BUY4 values and the card 8 bill maths (2,997 x 0.8 = 2,397.60; 3,696 x 0.7 = 2,587.20; difference 189.60); no free shipping, compare-at or struck prices (the delivery slot stays off); Velista calls carry no digits or rupee sign; hands only, no text in any picture; one product per picture; no real channel, brand or person imitated; card 9's 'rectangular step-cut' is the lock's emerald cut, kept out of the prompt so the stone does not turn green. truth: patched bible saved as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-naira-scroll/81f6e48f-a340-5398-99b2-f7e22fb69d37/scratchpad/k03truth/k03_truth.json (patch.py in the same folder).

ads.title: Rematch: the replay that proves it
ads.variant: rhodium silver tone (the only variant, 23 units); never beside the gold-tone twin
ads.headline: ONE DROP IS MILK.
ads.beat: scared of the shower? watch which drop stays.
ads.picture: The rematch opens on a freeze-frame replay. On a deep plum shamiana, a hand at the top of the frame lifts the necklace out of the paraat by both strands, so the smooth snake chain falls in a long narrow V to the stone hanging straight from its bail. One drop of milk has just let go of the lowest prong and hangs in the air on a breaking thread; straight below, the crown of the drop before stands frozen in the milk. Three moments, one frame: one drop has landed, one is falling, and the clear 10 mm cushion stays. The milk surface is a soft white band at the bottom. Field of view about 7 cm at the stone.
ads.prompt: Vertical 9:16 freeze-frame macro advertising photograph, side-on, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels: one continuous photograph fills the whole tall frame from the top edge to the bottom edge, never a square picture padded with flat colour, no frame within the frame. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Use it only for the snake chain's fine ridges and the 4 prongs; its bail junction is soft, so take the bail, sitting straight on the basket with no jump ring, from reference 1; ignore its green velvet. Reference 3 shows this exact piece worn at the base of the neck at true size (40 cm, 2 mm snake chain sitting at the base of the neck, as thick as a strand of spaghetti; the 10 mm cushion stone rests in the notch between the collarbones, about a little fingernail or half a Rs 1 coin, 5 times the chain's thickness): match that scale exactly; copy only the scale, never a face, a neck or a body. Preserve the necklace exactly: Rhodium silver tone. 1 smooth round snake chain, 2 mm thick, 40 cm plus a 5 cm curb-link extender and lobster clasp. At the front, 1 cushion-cut clear cubic zirconia, 10 mm (5x the chain's thickness), in an open 4-prong basket hung directly from 1 small bail. It must stay 1 stone in 4 prongs, the basket straight on the bail, never a halo, never an added jump ring, never a larger stone, never a sharp-cornered cut; the chain stays a smooth snake chain, never cable or box links; cool bright rhodium silver tone, never the gold-tone version. COUNT: exactly 1 stone (one, never two), exactly 4 prongs (four), exactly 1 bail and 0 jump rings between the bail and the basket. The chain, bail, basket, prongs, extender and clasp are all the same rhodium silver tone. Do not redesign or add anything. SCALE, set by her fingertips: field of view about 7 cm at the stone, so her two fingertips at the top edge are large in the frame, each about a fifth of the frame width; the stone is about 10 mm, the size of her little fingernail, about two thirds of the width of one fingertip pad and five times the chain's thickness; the chain is as thick as a strand of spaghetti. Never a larger stone: the stone is never as wide as her fingertip. SCENE: at the very top of the frame a young Indian bride's fingertips, with mehendi dots and a short bare nail, hold the necklace up by both strands out of a wide polished brass paraat, a plain round platter with a rolled rim and no engraving, filled with milky water, so the two smooth strands fall in a long narrow V to the stone, which hangs straight from its bail just below the centre of the frame; THREE MOMENTS IN ONE FROZEN FRAME: one drop of white milk, about half the stone's height, has just let go of the lowest prong and hangs in the air a few millimetres below the basket, joined to the prong tip only by a breaking hair-thin thread of milk, its top drawn up into a point, milky white with a translucent bluish edge, plainly liquid, never a smooth opaque pearl or bead; nothing white touches the stone; and straight below it, where the drop before it landed, a small crown of milk stands frozen up out of the milky surface at the bottom of the frame. The chain carries only a thin wet sheen, never beads or droplets. The milky surface is a soft rippling white band across the bottom of the frame. Background: deep plum velvet shamiana, dark and far out of focus. The stone is the brightest point in the frame. Above and left of the hanging chain, the same deep plum velvet falls into soft shadow, real fabric texture right up to the top edge, quiet enough for a headline; the milky band along the bottom edge stays plain apart from the one small crown, for the price card. LIGHT: two lights only. One soft cool-neutral key from the left; one small hard specular spot from behind right fires the stone with crisp white sparkle, draws a bright line along the snake chain and makes the falling drop's edge glow. True contact where her fingertips pinch the chain, with a small true contact shadow on the skin. Natural film grain, editorial demi-fine jewellery campaign quality. Only fingertips and hands: no face, no eyes, no eyebrows, no head. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark anywhere, nothing written in the mehendi. One product only: this one necklace is the only jewellery in the frame; no star glints, no rainbow flare.

ads.primaryText: Waterproof? It just came out of a paraat of milk. Any three, 20% off with BUY3. One drop falls; the other is a 10 mm cubic zirconia, and it stays. Free insured shipping, cash on delivery.
ads.motion: Kling 3.0 image-to-video from the approved still, 5 s, locked macro camera; nothing is composited (hard rule): the pendant, bail, prongs and chain are the still's own pixels and never move, swing or change, and any clip where they do is rejected. 0.0-1.4 s: the hair-thin thread snaps and the drop falls out through the brackets. 1.4-2.6 s: it lands in the milk band beside the frozen crown and throws a second small crown. 2.6-4.0 s: the stone hangs alone; one soft highlight slides across its table. HTML: at 2.0 s leader 1 follows the drop down and its label flips from 'MILK · FALLS OFF' to 'MILK · GONE'; at 3.0 s 'CUBIC ZIRCONIA · 10 MM · STAYS' draws on and the freeze brackets snap tight to the stone. 4.0-5.0 s: hold, card up.
ads.risk: The bead of milk merging into the stone or reading as a second stone, a jump ring sneaking in between bail and basket, the stone swelling past 10 mm, and in motion the pendant swinging. No take B (learnings 16). The drop is detached and plainly liquid, never an opaque bead on the prong; reject any frame where milk touches the stone or the drop reads as a second stone or a pearl. Nothing is composited.
ads.why10: It answers 'is it really waterproof, and what is that stone?' with one honest replay: the milk falls, the cubic zirconia stays. In motion the proof plays out in real time, which no claims panel can do. Silver on plum keeps the clear stone the brightest point, the way the account's winners did.

ads.picture: Day five of the wedding, and the search ends with one fingertip. The camera sits at the milk line, so the paraat becomes a calm white sea at dusk: a flat white horizon across the lower third, oxblood darkness above, two fairy lights like distant ships. Exactly one fingertip rises a few centimetres out of the milk like a lighthouse, and the barrel charm rests on top of it, the box chain sliding off both sides back into the white. Milk rings spread from where the finger broke the surface. Three pavé bands between two polished ribs catch pinpoints of light. Field of view about 6 cm, so the charm is two thirds of the fingertip's width.
